record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.context_brief: predicting Morse indices after birth surgery
record.original_question: Consider a one-parameter family of real analytic functions or polynomials f_τ:(C^n,R^n)->(C,R), for real τ in (-ε,ε), realizing a Morse birth surgery: for τ<0 there are two complex-conjugate critical points, these collide at an A_2 point as τ tends to 0, and then they reappear as two real Morse critical points of neighboring Morse indices. Is there a convenient topological characteristic of f_{-ε} that predicts the integer Morse indices of the two newborn real critical points, not just the parity of the greater index obtained from the sign of an intersection number of conjugate vanishing cycles?

evidence.quote:
Consider an one-parametric family of real analytic
functions (or just polynomials) fτ : ( Cn, Rn) → (C, R), τ ∈ (− ε, ε)
realizing a Morse birth surgery: the functions fτ , τ < 0, have two
complex conjugate critical points which collide in a point of type A2
when τ tends to 0, and after that reappear as two real Morse critical
points of some two neighboring Morse indices.
Problem 1F : is there any convenient topological characteristic of the
function f−ε which allows us to predict these indices?

Then the
sign of their intersection number is well-deﬁned and allows us to guess
the parity of the greater newborn critical point, see [15], [18]. But h ow
can we predict the integer index?

artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found. Related recent work (e.g. the classification of degree-three Morse polynomials on $\mathbb{R}^3$) develops combinatorial tools around Morse surgeries, local monodromy and Picard–Lefschetz theory, but only the parity of the larger Morse index is recovered from the sign of the intersection number of conjugate vanishing cycles; no topological characteristic predicting the integer indices appears to be known.

status_evidence.title: Isotopy classification of Morse polynomials of degree three on R^3
status_evidence.snippet: Uses Morse surgeries, local monodromy and Picard–Lefschetz theory; sign of intersection index of conjugate vanishing cycles predicts parities of Morse indices of newborn real critical points.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work continues to use only the parity-level prediction from intersection signs, with no integer-index characteristic given.
